teach.text: Say **مَرْحَبًا** (marhaban) for “hello.” You can also greet someone with **السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ** (as-salaamu 'alaykum), meaning “peace be upon you.” The reply is **وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ** (wa 'alaykumu s-salaam), “and upon you peace.”
Say **صَبَاحُ الْخَيْرِ** (sabaaHu l-khayr) for “good morning” and **مَسَاءُ الْخَيْرِ** (masaa'u l-khayr) for “good evening.”
Use **مَعَ السَّلَامَةِ** (ma'a s-salaama) to say “goodbye.” Say **شُكْرًا** (shukran) for “thank you” and **عَفْوًا** ('afwan) for “you're welcome.”
Use **مِنْ فَضْلِكَ** (min faDlika) to say “please.” It is addressed to one male.

practice.explain: صَبَاحُ الْخَيْرِ means “good morning.” مَسَاءُ الْخَيْرِ means “good evening.”
شُكْرًا is the Arabic phrase for “thank you.”
مَرْحَبًا means “hello” and is pronounced marhaban.

teach.text: **أَنَا** (ana) means “I.” **أَنْتَ** (anta) means “you” when speaking to one male. **أَنْتِ** (anti) means “you” when speaking to one female.
**هُوَ** (huwa) means “he,” and **هِيَ** (hiya) means “she.” These forms refer to one person.

**اِسْمِي** (ismii) means “my name.” For example, **اِسْمِي سَارَة** (ismii saara) means “My name is Sarah.” Names are written here without their final case vowel, as people normally say them when speaking.
Ask a male **مَا اسْمُكَ؟** (maa smuka?), “What is your name?” Ask a female **مَا اسْمُكِ؟** (maa smuki?). The first vowel of اِسْمُكَ is dropped after مَا, so you say maa smuka, not maa ismuka.
**أَنَا طَالِبٌ** (ana Taalib) means “I am a male student.” **أَنَا طَالِبَةٌ** (ana Taaliba) means “I am a female student.”

teach.text: Ask one male **مِنْ أَيْنَ أَنْتَ؟** (min ayna anta?) to mean “Where are you from?”
Say **أَنَا مِنْ …** (ana min …) to mean “I am from …” Add a country after مِنْ.
**مِصْر** (miSr) means Egypt. **الْأُرْدُن** (al-urdunn) means Jordan. Country names are shown in their basic form, without a final case vowel.
**فَرَنْسَا** (faransaa) means France. For example, **أَنَا مِنْ فَرَنْسَا** means “I am from France.”

مِصْر is the Arabic name for Egypt.
